title: Chat request flow
subject: POST /api/chat in a sample FastAPI backend
summary:
A signed-in user sends a message. Middleware verifies the JWT, the route embeds the message, pulls the closest memories from Postgres (pgvector), and streams a Claude reply back as server-sent events.

When the stream ends, the full reply is saved to the messages table.
limits: Static read of the code only. No runtime values were captured.
Prompt caching and retries are not implemented in this sample.

metadata.summary: Entry point. The mobile app posts a JSON body with the message and session id, plus a Bearer token.

example.message: what did I say about my trip?

notes: The router is mounted with prefix /api, so the route path /chat becomes /api/chat.

metadata.summary: Runs before every route. It strips the Bearer prefix, decodes the JWT, and stores the claims on request.state.user. A bad token returns 401 at once.

outputs.name: request.state.user
outputs.desc: Decoded JWT claims, for example sub

gotchas: BaseHTTPMiddleware wraps streaming responses; heavy middleware here can delay the first SSE byte.

metadata.summary: Decodes and checks the JWT signature and expiry with the shared secret.
metadata.code:
def verify_token(token: str) -> dict:
    return jwt.decode(token, JWT_SECRET, algorithms=["HS256"])
gotchas: The default "dev-secret" makes tokens forgeable if JWT_SECRET is not set in production.

metadata.summary: The route handler. It reads the user from request.state, gets memory context, starts the model stream, and returns it as server-sent events.
metadata.signature: async def chat_endpoint(body: ChatRequest, request: Request)
metadata.code:
async def chat_endpoint(body: ChatRequest, request: Request):
    user = request.state.user
    chunks = await retrieve_context(user["sub"], body.message, k=5)
    stream = generate(body.message, chunks)
    ...
    return StreamingResponse(sse(), media_type="text/event-stream")

metadata.summary: Embeds the message, queries the memories table by cosine distance, and keeps rows with score at or above MIN_SCORE.
metadata.details: pgvector's <=> operator returns cosine distance, so the query computes score = 1 - distance. The LIMIT runs before the score filter, so the function can return fewer than k rows.
metadata.signature: async def retrieve_context(user_id: str, text: str, k: int = 5) -> list[str]
metadata.code:
async def retrieve_context(user_id: str, text: str, k: int = 5) -> list[str]:
    vec = await embed(text)
    pool = await get_pool()
    rows = await pool.fetch(
        "SELECT content, 1 - (embedding <=> $1) AS score FROM memories "
        "WHERE user_id = $2 ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 LIMIT $3",
        vec, user_id, k,
    )
    return [r["content"] for r in rows if r["score"] >= MIN_SCORE]
gotchas: asyncpg needs a pgvector codec registered to send a Python list as a vector; without it the query fails.

metadata.summary: Calls the OpenAI embeddings endpoint for one string and returns the vector.
metadata.code:
async def embed(text: str) -> list[float]:
    res = await client.embeddings.create(model=EMBED_MODEL, input=text)
    return res.data[0].embedding

metadata.summary: Creates one shared connection pool on first use and returns it after that.
gotchas: Two first requests at the same time can both create a pool; there is no lock.

metadata.summary: Hosted embedding model. One HTTPS call per chat turn.
Stores memory embeddings for retrieval and the chat history.
notes: ORDER BY embedding <=> $1 uses an index only if an ivfflat or hnsw index exists with cosine ops.

metadata.summary: Builds a system prompt with the memories and streams text tokens from the Messages API.
metadata.signature: async def generate(message: str, chunks: list[str])
metadata.code:
async def generate(message: str, chunks: list[str]):
    memories = "\n".join(f"- {c}" for c in chunks)
    async with client.messages.stream(
        model=MODEL,
        max_tokens=800,
        temperature=0.7,
        system=f"{SYSTEM}\n\nMemories:\n{memories}",
        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": message}],
    ) as stream:
        async for text in stream.text_stream:
            yield text
gotchas: Only the current message is sent; earlier turns of the session are not included.

metadata.summary: Hosted model that streams the reply as server-sent events, which the SDK exposes as text_stream.
Inner generator. It forwards each token as an SSE event and collects the full reply. After the last token it saves the turn.
metadata.code:
async def sse():
        reply = []
        async for token in stream:
            reply.append(token)
            yield f"data: {token}\n\n"
        await save_message(body.session_id, body.message, "".join(reply))
gotchas: If the client disconnects mid-stream, the generator stops and the reply is never saved.

metadata.summary: Writes the user text and the full reply to the messages table.
metadata.signature: async def save_message(session_id: str, user_text: str, reply: str) -> None

metadata.summary: The app renders tokens as they arrive. The stream closes after the last token.
